title: Advance Tax Due 15 December 2026: How Much to Pay and Interest Rules
excerpt: The third advance tax instalment for tax year 2026-27 is due on 15 December. Who must pay, how to work out the 75% figure, the new section 424/425 interest rules and how to pay.
body:
The third advance tax instalment for tax year 2026-27 is due on **Tuesday, 15 December 2026**. By that date, you should have paid at least 75% of your estimated tax for the year. This is the first December instalment under the new Income-tax Act, 2025, so the section numbers have changed, but the basic rules work the way they always have.

## What advance tax is

Advance tax means paying income tax during the year, as you earn, instead of in one go when you file your return. Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, the liability is in **section 403** (old section 207). The interest for paying late or too little is in **sections 424 and 425** (old sections 234B and 234C).

## Who has to pay

You have to pay advance tax if your estimated tax for the year is **₹10,000 or more** after subtracting TDS and TCS. This usually covers:

- Business owners and professionals
- Freelancers and consultants whose clients deduct little or no TDS
- Salaried people with large other income, such as rent, interest, capital gains or dividends
- Companies and LLPs, whatever their size

**Senior citizens get an exemption.** A resident individual aged 60 or more during the tax year does not have to pay advance tax, provided they have no income from business or profession. A senior citizen who runs a business or practises a profession still has to pay.

If you only earn a salary and your employer deducts TDS correctly, you usually do not need to pay advance tax.

## The four instalments for tax year 2026-27

Each due date has a minimum share of your total estimated tax that must be paid by then. The shares are cumulative:

- **15 June 2026**: at least 15%
- **15 September 2026**: at least 45%
- **15 December 2026**: at least 75%
- **15 March 2027**: 100%

For example, say your estimated tax for the year is ₹4,00,000 after TDS. By 15 December you should have paid at least ₹3,00,000 in total. If you paid ₹1,80,000 by September, you now need to pay ₹1,20,000.

## Small businesses on presumptive taxation

The old presumptive schemes under sections 44AD and 44ADA are now in **section 58** of the new Act. If you declare income under this scheme, you can pay your whole advance tax in **one instalment by 15 March 2027**. You do not need to pay in December.

This relief applies only to the presumptive scheme. If you keep regular books and declare actual profits, the four-instalment schedule applies to you.

## How to work out your December payment

- Estimate your income for the full year, from April 2026 to March 2027. Use actual figures up to November and a fair projection for the rest.
- Include all income heads: business profit, salary, rent, interest, capital gains already booked, and dividends.
- Apply the tax regime you expect to use. The new regime is the default.
- Subtract TDS and TCS already deducted or expected. Check your Form 26AS and AIS for this.
- Pay 75% of the result, minus what you have already paid this year.

If the festive season boosted your sales, revise your estimate upwards now rather than in March.

## What happens if you pay late or too little

**Interest for deferment (section 425).** If your cumulative payment by a due date is less than the required share, you pay simple interest of 1% a month on the shortfall. For the June, September and December instalments, this works out to 3% of the shortfall for each. For the March instalment, it is 1%. A small margin is allowed for the first two instalments: no interest applies if you paid at least 12% by 15 June and at least 36% by 15 September.

**Interest for default (section 424).** If you pay less than 90% of your final tax by the end of the tax year, or pay nothing, you also pay simple interest of 1% for every month or part of a month. This runs from 1 April 2027 until you pay the tax.

There is some relief for income you could not have predicted, such as capital gains, dividends, or the first year of a new business. Section 425 interest does not apply to that income if you pay the tax on it in the instalments that follow, or by 31 March.

**Missed June or September?** Pay your full 75% by 15 December. The interest already charged for the earlier shortfalls stays, but paying now stops the December interest from adding to it and keeps the section 424 interest down.

## How to pay

Pay online through the **e-Pay Tax** service on the income-tax e-filing portal. Choose the Income-tax Act, 2025 and tax year 2026-27, and select **Advance Tax** as the payment type. Make sure you don't select self-assessment tax by mistake. You can pay by net banking, debit card, UPI or at an authorised bank. Keep the challan receipt so the payment is easy to match when you file your return.
